newsitem.title: UK: Matthew Clark cider market share fell 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Matthew Clark cider market share fell 4 pct.

text.p: British cider maker Matthew Clark Plc, whose share price more than halved after it issued a profit warning last September, said on Wednesday its share of the cider market fell to 37 percent from 41 percent in the year to April.

The company, whose business has been hit by the huge growth in so-called "alcopops" and a severe industry-wide price war, reported pretax profits before exceptional items of 40.6 million pounds ($68.2 million) in the year to April 30, off four percent from last year's 42.3 million.
The company also announced an unchanged total dividend of 24 pence per share.

"We have addressed the issues of the past year by putting robust marketing and commercial plans in place to stabilise our cider business and return it to growth over the medium and long term," chief executive Peter Aikens said in a statement.

The company said it intends to rebuild its position in the cider market within its marketing and business plan for the next three years. While it does not expect an "overnight recovery" in shareholder value, it does see a "steady and well managed recovery".

Sales of Diamond White, the Diamond range and K Cider were hit by the unprecedented growth in "alcopops" -- alcoholic lemonades and sodas -- with volumes down 26 percent over the year. This had an adverse impact of 12 million pounds.

As well as "alcopops" the other setback facing the company was the developing price war with its main competitor -- H.P. Bulmer Holdings Plc -- in the cider industry. This was partly responsible for a further shortfall in profits of 14 million pounds.
Bulmer last week reported that its share of the cider market had grown to 54.5 percent, its highest level for over 30 years.
These two issues led to Matthew Clark's cider volumes falling by 13 percent over the year in a market down by three percent. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
